AGRICULTURE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #7
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which part holds the head of the scarecrow? (1 mark)
   A. The fence
   B. The top of the pole
   C. The dry grass on the ground
   D. The tin

2. How fine should the soil in the seedbed be? (1 mark)
   A. Full of big clods
   B. Wet like mud
   C. Crumbly like brown sugar
   D. Hard like stone

3. What is a grafted seedling? (1 mark)
   A. A young tree joined with a branch from a good tree
   B. A dead plant
   C. A plant grown in water
   D. A seed in a bag

4. Which method removes dry dirt from the floor with a broom? (1 mark)
   A. Washing
   B. Dusting
   C. Mopping
   D. Sweeping

5. How do you know millet is ready to harvest? (1 mark)
   A. The heads turn brown and the grains are hard
   B. The seeds are wet
   C. The plant flowers
   D. The plants are green and soft

6. Which is the best material for stuffing a scarecrow? (1 mark)
   A. Wet mud
   B. Stones
   C. Glass
   D. Dry grass

7. Which is the safest way to make holes or dig for scarecrow parts? (1 mark)
   A. Use broken glass
   B. Ask an adult to help
   C. Play with the tools
   D. Use bare hands on sharp tools

8. What is the purpose of sticks at the bottom of the compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. They make it look neat
   B. They add plant food
   C. They let air move through the heap
   D. They keep the heap dry forever

9. What does sowing mean? (1 mark)
   A. Cutting a crop
   B. Storing seeds
   C. Watering a crop
   D. Putting seeds into the soil so they can grow

10. Why is it best to plant fruit varieties that suit the local climate? (1 mark)
   A. They need no water
   B. They never get pests
   C. They grow and fruit better
   D. They cost more

11. Which PPE protects the hands? (1 mark)
   A. Headgear
   B. Gumboots
   C. Gloves
   D. Dust mask

12. Which is recycling? (1 mark)
   A. Turning used material into something new
   B. Sending it to sea
   C. Burying it
   D. Burning it

13. Which of these fruits grows on a woody tree? (1 mark)
   A. Mango
   B. Blackberry
   C. Passion fruit
   D. Grapes

14. How does the tippy tap release water? (1 mark)
   A. By a battery
   B. A foot lever tips the container
   C. By a magnet
   D. By a switch

15. Which of these completes the farm cycle: animals, manure, ____? (1 mark)
   A. Roads
   B. Machines
   C. Bricks
   D. Crops

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Name three safety rules when using gas for cooking. (3 marks)

17. Plan a weekly cleaning schedule for the classroom using dusting, sweeping, mopping and refuse disposal. (5 marks)

18. Explain how compost conserves both soil and the environment. (5 marks)

19. Give two reasons why soil should be conserved. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #7 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — The top of the pole
   The head is fixed to the top of the long pole.

2. C — Crumbly like brown sugar
   Fine crumbly soil lets seeds come up easily.

3. A — A young tree joined with a branch from a good tree
   Grafted trees give good quality fruit sooner.

4. D — Sweeping
   Sweeping uses a broom.

5. A — The heads turn brown and the grains are hard
   Ripe grain is hard and dry.

6. D — Dry grass
   Dry grass is light and easy to use.

7. B — Ask an adult to help
   Safety comes first.

8. C — They let air move through the heap
   Air helps the tiny living things rot the wastes.

9. D — Putting seeds into the soil so they can grow
   Sowing is planting seeds.

10. C — They grow and fruit better
   Wrong climate gives poor growth.

11. C — Gloves
   Gloves cover the hands.

12. A — Turning used material into something new
   Recycling reuses materials.

13. A — Mango
   Mango grows on a woody tree.

14. B — A foot lever tips the container
   Pushing the lever tips the container.

15. D — Crops
   Manure feeds crops, and crops feed animals.

SECTION B
----
16. (3 marks)
   Answer: Keep the cylinder upright and away from fire; close the valve after use; if you smell gas open windows and do not light a flame.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

17. (5 marks)
   Answer: A table of days with jobs for each learner group: Monday dusting, Tuesday sweeping, Wednesday mopping, and refuse disposal each day, with tools and safety measures.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for jobs, 1 for tools, 1 for safety, 1 for fairness of sharing.

18. (5 marks)
   Answer: It adds food to the soil and makes it firm so it is not washed easily. It reuses wastes instead of leaving them as rubbish, and it reduces the need for factory fertiliser.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for soil, 2 marks for environment, 1 mark for a clear example.

19. (2 marks)
   Answer: Soil grows our food, and if it is washed away or made poor the crops will fail.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for soil grows food, 1 mark for erosion or loss of plant food.
